metadata.title: Symbol of the Guanacaste Skies | Scarlet Macaw
metadata.description: The health of the dry forest rests on the wings of the Scarlet Macaw. Discover its ecology, threats, and recovery efforts.

hero.title: Symbol of the Guanacaste Skies
hero.subtitle: The health of the tropical dry forest rests on its wings. Discover the history, the threats, and the rebirth of the Scarlet Macaw.

introduction.title: Much more than bright colors
introduction.body: The Ara macao is a creature of extreme intelligence and strong social structure. They live for over 50 years and mate for life, meaning the loss of a single individual affects entire generations and the natural dynamics of their flock.

ecology.title: The Architects of the Forest
ecology.body: They don't interact passively with their environment; they are forest sowers. By feeding on heavy fruits like the mountain almond, guanacaste, and ceiba, they spread their seeds over immense distances. Protecting the macaw means protecting the lungs of the dry tropics.

threats.title: On the edge of silence
threats.body: At the end of the 20th century, Guanacaste almost lost its flagship bird. Widespread deforestation destroyed their natural nesting sites. Simultaneously, a ruthless black market massively poached their nests, kidnapping chicks to force them into national and international captivity.

recovery.title: The Red Rebirth
recovery.body: Today, thanks to the strict protection of forestry laws and the heroic efforts of park rangers, NGOs, and community brigades, the population has begun to recover. Slowly, the skies of Guanacaste are once again colored with hope.

ethics.title: Be a silent visitor
ethics.rule1Desc: Do not attempt to feed them. Their role is to eat forest fruits to spread seeds.
ethics.rule2Desc: They were born to fly dozens of kilometers. Never support illegal captivity or buy wildlife.
ethics.rule3Desc: Avoid playing recorded macaw sounds to attract them (playback); this severely alters their natural behavior and causes stress.

cta.title: The forest still needs defenders
cta.body: Add your voice. Learn more, report wildlife trafficking to the authorities, and support the national sanctuaries that protect our tropical wealth.
